pages.description: Web presents workspace state and sends explicit actions to Server. Desktop supplies the native shell and selected-host transport; managers and Runner retain execution authority.
App composes authentication, startup, capability checks, recovery and hash-routed workspace pages. Lazy feature entry points keep heavy editors outside the initial route.
React holds selections, drafts and rendered projections. Server responses and manager events determine durable workspace state.
workspaceFetch and workspaceSocket select the browser or bundled Client transport. The selected host remains the destination of workspace operations.
Authentication and installation readiness gate the workspace. Onboarding presents observed setup progress before normal workspace navigation.
Feature clients correlate requests and reconcile live events. A disconnected or timed-out submission can have an unknown remote outcome.
Recovery keeps workspace failures visible and lets readers return to authoritative state without silently repeating work.
Workspace pages combine project selection, history and search. Project-file previews are reads against the selected project, not an independent filesystem authority.
Conversation views render authoritative chat items, requests and turn state. Session readers expose related agent history without becoming a second conversation store.
Supervision controls project monitor state into a conversation-linked view. The frontend contract must be distinguished from current Server execution support.
Provider catalogs supply identities, controls and account observations. Web displays readiness evidence rather than treating a configured account as proof that a launch can run.
Prompts, skills and MCP resources have distinct stores and editors. Launch selection captures resource choices; a library edit does not silently rewrite active work.
The builder translates canvas state into workflow definitions and validation feedback. A valid canvas is not evidence that an execution has completed.
Run views correlate accepted work with run events, outputs and failures. Runner owns execution; Web owns the readable projection and explicit controls.
Terminal panes attach to host-owned sessions and render streamed output through xterm. Pane visibility and socket connectivity are separate from process lifecycle.
Carrier projects messages, delegated work and delivery evidence into an inbox/outbox interface. Reading, delivery and acknowledgment are distinct events.
Connect views present devices, transfers, remote conversations and project comparisons. UI contracts alone do not qualify the corresponding host integration.
Vox presents call state and conversation links when voice capabilities are available. Media and call readiness remain separate from the visibility of the interface.
Settings combines local preferences with explicit host operations. Update presentation must preserve reviewed plans, blockers and restart consent.
The shared editor guard protects dirty or saving resource edits across navigation and browser unload.
Conversation content is untrusted data. Markdown and Mermaid use explicit rendering boundaries before content reaches the interface.
Use BBB components and Suite brand roles to make observed state, next actions and recovery understandable across themes and viewports.
Select checks by the owning module and its service dependencies. Fixture coverage demonstrates UI behavior; live qualification needs the actual owning services.
Screenshots show the real Web interface with simulated data. They illustrate structure and interaction states without asserting backend or provider readiness.
A retained component or fixture test establishes a frontend contract. Availability of its Server handlers and downstream services must be checked separately.
